en.yssttuph_title: You should sometimes tell time using proportional hours
en.yssttuph_nav_title: You should sometimes tell time using proportional hours
en.yssttuph_desc: Twelve hours of daylight, every day of the year.
en.yssttuph_p1: The moments that make up a dull day, or a sunny day, are not always equal amounts of time. This is no revelation, people realized this quite a long time ago. However, despite this eternal knowledge, this is something I could argue is largely forgotten in our day. Perhaps Daylight Savings is simply so effective at accounting for annual astrological changes that altering our schedules is simply unnecessary; but I think that as we've developed ways to have light, heat, and other necessities of the sun brought to the realm of inside: The status of the heavens has become something more along the lines of backdrop. Time seems, then, to be something that mostly occurs separately from our perceptions. 12 hours in the winter looks very different from 12 hours in the spring. It feels very… tacked-on, doesn't it?
en.yssttuph_h3_time-time-could-you-be-mine: Time, time, could you be mine?
en.yssttuph_p2: So, what if instead the day began not at some range between 4:00 AM and 8:00 AM, but at 0? What if it ends at 12? That's called Proportional Hours, the Fahrenheit of time.
en.yssttuph_p3: This gets tricky, but this is more or less how time was determined by some of the top civilizations of history. We all know the story since then, once we needed consistent time between locales for the sake of trains, for accurate measurement at sea, and other such things, time did have to change.
en.yssttuph_p4: But like, it can all be Unix Epoch underneath now. We don't lose any accuracy. It's like how customary units are defined in S.I. ones deep down.
en.yssttuph_p5: What we do lose is that time zones become the size of zip codes.
en.yssttuph_p6: Use the arrows to see how day time fluctuates over the year.
en.yssttuph_p7: This is not strictly useful for things like baking.
en.yssttuph_p8: However, it could be good for timing how much of your day you used doing something, or how much of your day is left. There's no rule that says you have to only use one system. With proportional hours, you'll always know where the sun is.
en.yssttuph_p9: Give it a try! 🕰 shaon.zmanim
